dataset_metadata.description: A large-scale corpus for long-form abstractive summarization consisting of scientific papers from arXiv.org. The dataset pairs the full-text body of academic articles with their corresponding abstracts, posing a challenge for models due to the significant length of the input discourse and the technical nature of the vocabulary.

schema_analysis.description: The full body text of the scientific paper, excluding the abstract.
The author-written abstract of the paper, serving as the ground-truth summary.
Newline-separated list of section headers present in the article.

structural_logic.relationships: The 'article' column serves as the source sequence, while the 'abstract' is the target sequence for summarization. 'section_names' provides structural metadata reflecting the hierarchy of the 'article' content.
structural_logic.label_dynamics: High compression ratio; the source text is often 30-40 times longer than the target abstract, requiring significant information extraction and synthesis.
structural_logic.potential_bottlenecks: Presence of LaTeX mathematical notation and citations can introduce noise; long-range dependencies exceed the context window of standard Transformer models (e.g., BERT/GPT-2) without sparse attention mechanisms.
